questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explain: Au comes from aurum, the Latin word for gold.

questions.question: How many bones are in the typical adult human body?
questions.explain: Babies are born with roughly 270 to 300 bones. Many fuse together as they grow, leaving 206 in a typical adult.

questions.question: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explain: Iron oxide, basically rust, in Martian dust and rocks gives Mars its reddish color.

questions.question: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
questions.explain: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets in the solar system combined.

questions.question: Which gas do plants absorb from the air for photosynthesis?
questions.explain: Plants take in carbon dioxide and water and use sunlight to turn them into sugar, releasing oxygen as a by-product.

questions.question: Which element has the atomic number 1?
questions.explain: An element's atomic number is its count of protons. Hydrogen has just one, and it's the most abundant element in the universe.

questions.question: Which part of the cell is known as its powerhouse?
questions.explain: Mitochondria produce most of a cell's ATP, the molecule cells use as their energy currency.

questions.question: At sea level, water boils at how many degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.explain: 212°F is the same as 100°C, the boiling point of water at standard sea-level pressure.

questions.question: Roughly how fast does light travel in a vacuum?
questions.explain: The speed of light is defined as exactly 299,792,458 meters per second, just under 300,000 km per second.

questions.question: Which mineral scores a 10, the maximum, on the Mohs hardness scale?
questions.explain: The Mohs scale ranks scratch resistance from talc at 1 to diamond at 10. Corundum, the mineral in rubies and sapphires, is a 9.

questions.question: Which spice comes from the stigmas of a crocus flower?
questions.explain: Saffron threads are the hand-picked stigmas of the saffron crocus, which is why it's one of the most expensive spices by weight.

questions.question: What is the capital of Australia?
questions.explain: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital, partly as a compromise in the rivalry between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.explain: The Pacific is both the largest and the deepest ocean, covering roughly a third of Earth's surface.

questions.question: What is the capital of Canada?
questions.explain: Queen Victoria chose Ottawa as the capital in 1857.

questions.question: Which country has the largest land area?
questions.explain: Russia covers over 17 million square kilometers and spans 11 time zones.

questions.question: Mount Everest sits on the border between Nepal and which other country?
questions.explain: Everest straddles the border between Nepal and China's Tibet Autonomous Region.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world by area?
questions.explain: Vatican City covers about 0.44 square kilometers and sits entirely inside the city of Rome.

questions.question: What is the capital of New Zealand?
questions.explain: Wellington replaced Auckland as New Zealand's capital in 1865.

questions.question: What is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explain: The Sahara covers about 9 million square kilometers. Only the cold polar deserts of Antarctica and the Arctic are bigger.

questions.question: Which river flows through Baghdad?
questions.explain: Baghdad sits on the Tigris. The Euphrates, its twin river, flows further to the west.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explain: Germany surrendered in May 1945, and Japan formally surrendered on September 2, 1945.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explain: George Washington served two terms, from 1789 to 1797.

questions.question: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.explain: Apollo 11 landed on July 20, 1969, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface.

questions.question: Which ship sank on its maiden voyage in 1912?
questions.explain: The Titanic struck an iceberg on the night of April 14, 1912 and sank early the next morning. More than 1,500 people died.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explain: The wall opened on November 9, 1989. Germany reunified less than a year later, in October 1990.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.explain: The Inca built Machu Picchu in the 15th century, high in the Andes of Peru.

questions.question: Who was the first person to travel into outer space?
questions.explain: Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth aboard Vostok 1 on April 12, 1961.

questions.question: In which year was the Magna Carta sealed?
questions.explain: King John sealed the Magna Carta at Runnymede in 1215, limiting the power of the English crown.

questions.question: How many strings does a standard guitar have?
questions.explain: A standard guitar has six strings, usually tuned E A D G B E from lowest to highest.

questions.question: Which band released the album Abbey Road?
questions.explain: The Beatles released Abbey Road in 1969. It's named after the London street where they recorded, and the cover shows them on its zebra crossing.

questions.question: In chess, which piece can only ever move diagonally?
questions.explain: A bishop moves any number of squares diagonally, so it stays on the same color for the whole game. The queen can move diagonally too, but not only diagonally.

questions.question: How many squares are on a standard chessboard?
questions.explain: A chessboard is an 8 by 8 grid, which makes 64 squares.

questions.question: Which company created the arcade game Pac-Man?
questions.explain: Namco released Pac-Man in 1980. It was designed by Toru Iwatani.

questions.question: In which year was the original PlayStation released in Japan?
questions.explain: The PlayStation launched in Japan on December 3, 1994, and reached North America in September 1995.

questions.question: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.explain: Leonardo da Vinci began the Mona Lisa in the early 1500s. It hangs in the Louvre in Paris.

questions.question: Who wrote Pride and Prejudice?
questions.explain: Jane Austen published Pride and Prejudice in 1813.

questions.question: Who wrote the novel Nineteen Eighty-Four?
questions.explain: George Orwell published Nineteen Eighty-Four in 1949.

questions.question: How many players does each soccer team have on the field at once?
questions.explain: Each side fields 11 players, including the goalkeeper.

questions.question: In golf, what is the term for finishing a hole one stroke under par?
questions.explain: One under par is a birdie, two under is an eagle, and one over is a bogey.

questions.question: How many points is a touchdown worth in American football, before the extra point?
questions.explain: A touchdown is 6 points. The team can then kick for 1 more point or try a two-point conversion.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 2016 Summer Olympics?
questions.explain: Rio de Janeiro hosted in 2016, the first Olympics held in South America.

questions.question: In basketball, how many points is a made shot from beyond the arc worth?
questions.explain: Shots from beyond the three-point line are worth 3. The NBA adopted the line in the 1979–80 season.

questions.question: What is the official distance of a marathon?
questions.explain: A marathon is 42.195 km, or 26.2 miles. The distance traces back to the course of the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.question: What is pi rounded to two decimal places?
questions.explain: Pi is 3.14159…, the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. Its digits never end or repeat.

questions.question: What is the square root of 144?
What is the only even prime number?
questions.explain: Every other even number can be divided by 2, so 2 is the only even number with no divisors besides 1 and itself.

questions.question: How is the decimal number 10 written in binary?
questions.explain: 1010 in binary means 8 + 0 + 2 + 0, which adds up to 10.

questions.question: How many bits are in a byte?
questions.explain: A byte is 8 bits, enough to represent 256 different values.

questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explain: HyperText Transfer Protocol. Tim Berners-Lee developed it at CERN starting in 1989.

questions.question: Which TCP port does HTTPS use by default?
questions.explain: HTTPS is HTTP over TLS and uses port 443 by default. Plain HTTP uses port 80.

questions.question: Who is often credited as the first computer programmer?
questions.explain: Ada Lovelace published an algorithm for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine in 1843.

questions.question: What is the largest mammal on Earth?
questions.explain: The blue whale is the largest animal known to have ever lived, reaching about 30 meters long.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explain: Two hearts pump blood through the gills and a third pumps it around the rest of the body.

questions.question: What is a group of lions called?
questions.explain: A pride is usually a group of related females, their cubs, and a few males.

questions.question: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.explain: Cheetahs can top 100 km/h, over 60 mph, in short sprints.

questions.question: What is the largest living bird?
questions.explain: The ostrich is the largest and heaviest living bird. It can't fly, but it can run at around 70 km/h.

questions.question: In Greek mythology, who is the king of the gods?
questions.explain: Zeus rules the gods from Mount Olympus as the god of the sky and thunder.

questions.question: In Norse mythology, what is the name of Thor's hammer?
questions.explain: Thor's hammer is Mjölnir. Gungnir is Odin's spear, and Draupnir is Odin's ring.

questions.question: What is the Roman name for the Greek god Ares?
questions.explain: Mars is the Roman god of war. The other options are Roman gods too: Mercury is Hermes, Jupiter is Zeus, and Vulcan is Hephaestus.

questions.question: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.explain: Guacamole is mashed avocado, a Mexican dish with roots in Aztec cuisine.

questions.question: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
questions.explain: Sound moves at about 1,480 meters per second in water, compared with about 343 in air at room temperature.

questions.question: The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
questions.explain: The wall is far too narrow to see from that distance. Apollo astronauts reported they couldn't make out any human-made structures from the Moon.

questions.question: Venus is the hottest planet in our solar system.
questions.explain: Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat, keeping the surface around 465°C, hotter than Mercury even though Mercury is closer to the Sun.

questions.question: Bats are blind.
questions.explain: All bats can see. Many species also use echolocation to hunt in the dark.

questions.question: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
questions.explain: Tall structures get hit over and over. The Empire State Building is struck about 20 to 25 times a year.

questions.question: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit.
questions.explain: Tomatoes develop from the flower's ovary and contain seeds, which makes them fruits. The U.S. Supreme Court still ruled them vegetables for tariff purposes in 1893.
